description: FIND-001 closure is INCOMPLETE: the behavioral-spec side is fixed (REQ-M2 verbatim states 'NOT call enqueue_task_descriptor', 'eliminates the previous spec's dequeue:false field', 'frozen task_descriptor shape stays unchanged'), but verification-architecture.md line 47 still carries the OLD contract: PROP-M2-dispatcher-in-process reads 'integration test: STEP 6 with reconciler item invokes reconcile in-process; no subprocess spawned; tasks/ descriptor has reconciler_report field'. There are TWO defects: (1) the clause 'tasks/ descriptor has reconciler_report field' directly contradicts REQ-M2(b) which forbids the enqueue AND contradicts REQ-M2 which explicitly preserves the frozen 7-key task_descriptor shape (skills/_shared/lib/step6_act.py:31-43 has keys {schema_version, pass_id, ts, picked, budget, proactive_loop_origin, slot} — no reconciler_report). (2) the PROP is testing for the presence of an artifact that REQ-M2 says MUST NOT EXIST. Under lean mode this creates two impossible-to-reconcile outcomes: either PROP-M2 tests the tasks/ descriptor (violates REQ-M2 → live-money double-execute risk resurfaces) OR the impl skips enqueue (PROP-M2 fails because no descriptor exists to inspect). This is the same class of defect FIND-001 iter-1 called out — the fix removed the ambiguity from behavioral-spec but re-introduced it in verification-architecture. Live-money impact: if a builder follows PROP-M2 verbatim, they will re-add descriptor-mutation code that duplicates reconciler execution via LAYER C dequeue.
